sources.title: Grid (Interactive Tabular Data and Layout Containers) Pattern
sources.version_or_commit: Live WAI-ARIA APG page; no numbered release shown (guidance, not a W3C Recommendation).
sources.locator: Data Grids For Presenting Tabular Information; Keyboard Interaction; Editing and Navigating Inside a Cell; WAI-ARIA Roles, States, and Properties.
sources.observed_operation: The pattern treats an editable/interactive data grid as a composite widget with one tab-sequence entry and author-managed focus among cells. It gives arrow/Home/End navigation; Enter or F2 enters cell editing; Escape restores grid navigation and may undo; selection and sort states are separate properties. It warns Control+End may reach the last DOM row rather than the last backend row when rows are dynamically added.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Every data cell is focusable or contains focusable content; nonfunctional header cells need not be focusable. Arrow keys belong to grid navigation only outside edit/widget interaction. Use row/column counts and indexes when rows or columns are hidden or absent from the DOM.
sources.applicability: Web accessibility authoring guidance; useful interaction model for a desktop grid, but a native app must map equivalent semantics through its platform accessibility API.

sources.title: Accessible Rich Internet Applications (WAI-ARIA) 1.2
sources.version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation, 2023-06-06 (version-pinned URL).
sources.locator: Roles grid and table; aria-rowcount / aria-rowindex / aria-colcount / aria-colindex; aria-selected; aria-sort; aria-readonly.
sources.observed_operation: Normative web accessibility semantics distinguish interactive grid from noninteractive table; partial DOM rows/columns can expose full counts and logical indexes. aria-selected indicates selection; aria-sort indicates sort order on a table/grid header; aria-readonly indicates editability, not navigability.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: For partial DOM, aria-rowcount/colcount represent full available totals (use -1 when unknown), with 1-based indexes for present rows/cells. aria-sort belongs on headers and should be on at most one header per grid. Apply only semantic states matching actual behavior.
sources.applicability: Normative WAI-ARIA requirements for web content/host languages; not a direct native desktop API contract.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation, 2024-12-12 (version-pinned URL).
sources.locator: Success Criteria 2.1.1 Keyboard (A), 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA), 3.3.1 Error Identification (A), and 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA).
sources.observed_operation: Normative criteria require keyboard operation for all functionality, a visible focus indicator, text identification of input errors, and programmatically determinable status messages when markup-based status updates do not receive focus.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WCAG is scoped to web content; the exact criteria are not asserted as the governing legal standard for this unspecified desktop app. Their user outcomes remain design checks; native API equivalents and applicable obligations need an owner/platform decision.
sources.applicability: Use as a web-content target if that is the chosen delivery surface; otherwise treat as a useful baseline and verify OS accessibility contracts.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 3.3.1: Error Identification
sources.version_or_commit: Living WAI Understanding document; no pinned edition shown; consulted 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Intent and error identification examples, especially lines/sections requiring the identity of the item in error and describing errors in text.
sources.observed_operation: WAI explanatory guidance says an error description should provide its nature and identity of the item in error; text can be supplemented by color or an icon. An error list, inline message, alert, or dialog can be suitable depending on the situation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Informative explanation, not the normative WCAG text. HTML native validation may return focus to first invalid field but can show generic/nonpermanent messages and expose only the first error at a time.
sources.applicability: Supports a record-and-field-addressable error summary plus inline field explanation; native desktop implementation should expose equivalent text and focus behavior.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 4.1.3: Status Messages
sources.version_or_commit: Living WAI Understanding document; no pinned edition shown; consulted 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Intent and definition of status messages; distinctions between result-set content and brief search completion/status text.
sources.observed_operation: Status updates that do not take focus may be exposed to assistive technology without moving focus. WAI distinguishes the actual result list from a brief message such as result count or search completion.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Applies to markup-language content. Do not treat every background record change as a status message; expose meaningful operation state/errors without flooding or interrupting the user.
sources.applicability: Guides aggregate announcements for filter/save/error status; platform-native notification/event mechanism must be tested if this is a native desktop application.

sources.title: JavaScript Grid: Accessibility - AG Grid
sources.version_or_commit: AG Grid 36.2.0, explicitly shown on page.
sources.locator: ARIA Attributes; Ensure DOM Element order; Disable Group Sticky Rows; Ensure all grid elements are always rendered; Known Limitations.
sources.observed_operation: AG Grid uses row/column virtualization for performance. Its guidance recommends DOM order, avoiding sticky group rows for consistent indices, and disabling row/column virtualization or using pagination to ensure screen readers can inspect all rendered grid elements; disabling virtualization can grow DOM and slow rendering. It reports differences between screen-reader interpretation and recommends testing combinations.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: These are AG Grid vendor recommendations, not a universal ARIA rule. The 'disable virtualization' advice is explicitly balanced against performance and suggests pagination when needed.
sources.applicability: Useful implementation evidence and a warning about AT behavior; not a direct dependency recommendation for a native desktop console.

sources.locator: Row IDs section and getRowId guidance.
sources.observed_operation: AG Grid strongly recommends a pure getRowId function returning the same unique string for a given row; duplicate IDs are disallowed. Its update docs show selection/state is maintained across updates when IDs are supplied.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Without supplied IDs, some row data replacement paths rebuild state; behavior is specific to AG Grid's data update model.
sources.applicability: Supports stable record keys across updates/sorting; does not determine the application's identity scheme.

sources.title: Data Grid - Accessibility - MUI X
sources.version_or_commit: Current MUI X documentation; page has no explicit release label in the retrieved text.

sources.title: Grid (Interactive Tabular Data and Layout Containers) Pattern
sources.version_or_commit: Live WAI-ARIA APG page; no numbered release shown (guidance, not a W3C Recommendation).
sources.locator: Data Grids For Presenting Tabular Information; Keyboard Interaction; Editing and Navigating Inside a Cell; WAI-ARIA Roles, States, and Properties.
sources.observed_operation: The pattern treats an editable/interactive data grid as a composite widget with one tab-sequence entry and author-managed focus among cells. It gives arrow/Home/End navigation; Enter or F2 enters cell editing; Escape restores grid navigation and may undo; selection and sort states are separate properties. It warns Control+End may reach the last DOM row rather than the last backend row when rows are dynamically added.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Every data cell is focusable or contains focusable content; nonfunctional header cells need not be focusable. Arrow keys belong to grid navigation only outside edit/widget interaction. Use row/column counts and indexes when rows or columns are hidden or absent from the DOM.
sources.applicability: Web accessibility authoring guidance; useful interaction model for a desktop grid, but a native app must map equivalent semantics through its platform accessibility API.

critic_verification.review_note: Confirmed APG composite focus model, navigation/edit key split, and warning that an end command can stop at the last loaded DOM row.

sources.title: Accessible Rich Internet Applications (WAI-ARIA) 1.2
sources.version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation, 2023-06-06 (version-pinned URL).
sources.locator: Roles grid and table; aria-rowcount / aria-rowindex / aria-colcount / aria-colindex; aria-selected; aria-sort; aria-readonly.
sources.observed_operation: Normative web accessibility semantics distinguish interactive grid from noninteractive table; partial DOM rows/columns can expose full counts and logical indexes. aria-selected indicates selection; aria-sort indicates sort order on a table/grid header; aria-readonly indicates editability, not navigability.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: For partial DOM, aria-rowcount/colcount represent full available totals (use -1 when unknown), with 1-based indexes for present rows/cells. aria-sort belongs on headers and should be on at most one header per grid. Apply only semantic states matching actual behavior.
sources.applicability: Normative WAI-ARIA requirements for web content/host languages; not a direct native desktop API contract.

critic_verification.review_note: Confirmed W3C Recommendation date and partial-DOM row count/index requirements; web semantics do not prescribe native APIs.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation, 2024-12-12 (version-pinned URL).
sources.locator: Success Criteria 2.1.1 Keyboard (A), 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA), 3.3.1 Error Identification (A), and 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA).
sources.observed_operation: Normative criteria require keyboard operation for all functionality, a visible focus indicator, text identification of input errors, and programmatically determinable status messages when markup-based status updates do not receive focus.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WCAG is scoped to web content; the exact criteria are not asserted as the governing legal standard for this unspecified desktop app. Their user outcomes remain design checks; native API equivalents and applicable obligations need an owner/platform decision.
sources.applicability: Use as a web-content target if that is the chosen delivery surface; otherwise treat as a useful baseline and verify OS accessibility contracts.

critic_verification.review_note: Confirmed WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.1 text identification requirement and web scope.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 3.3.1: Error Identification
sources.version_or_commit: Living WAI Understanding document; no pinned edition shown; consulted 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Intent and error identification examples, especially lines/sections requiring the identity of the item in error and describing errors in text.
sources.observed_operation: WAI explanatory guidance says an error description should provide its nature and identity of the item in error; text can be supplemented by color or an icon. An error list, inline message, alert, or dialog can be suitable depending on the situation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Informative explanation, not the normative WCAG text. HTML native validation may return focus to first invalid field but can show generic/nonpermanent messages and expose only the first error at a time.
sources.applicability: Supports a record-and-field-addressable error summary plus inline field explanation; native desktop implementation should expose equivalent text and focus behavior.

critic_verification.review_note: Confirmed WAI explanation requires nature and identity of the item in error; correction suggestions are a separate criterion.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 4.1.3: Status Messages
sources.version_or_commit: Living WAI Understanding document; no pinned edition shown; consulted 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Intent and definition of status messages; distinctions between result-set content and brief search completion/status text.
sources.observed_operation: Status updates that do not take focus may be exposed to assistive technology without moving focus. WAI distinguishes the actual result list from a brief message such as result count or search completion.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Applies to markup-language content. Do not treat every background record change as a status message; expose meaningful operation state/errors without flooding or interrupting the user.
sources.applicability: Guides aggregate announcements for filter/save/error status; platform-native notification/event mechanism must be tested if this is a native desktop application.

critic_verification.review_note: Confirmed markup status messages can be announced without focus; no basis to map this directly to unspecified native APIs.

sources.title: Grid (Interactive Tabular Data and Layout Containers) Pattern
sources.version_or_commit: Live WAI-ARIA APG page; no numbered release shown (guidance, not a W3C Recommendation).
sources.locator: Data Grids For Presenting Tabular Information; Keyboard Interaction; Editing and Navigating Inside a Cell; WAI-ARIA Roles, States, and Properties.
sources.observed_operation: The pattern treats an editable/interactive data grid as a composite widget with one tab-sequence entry and author-managed focus among cells. It gives arrow/Home/End navigation; Enter or F2 enters cell editing; Escape restores grid navigation and may undo; selection and sort states are separate properties. It warns Control+End may reach the last DOM row rather than the last backend row when rows are dynamically added.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Every data cell is focusable or contains focusable content; nonfunctional header cells need not be focusable. Arrow keys belong to grid navigation only outside edit/widget interaction. Use row/column counts and indexes when rows or columns are hidden or absent from the DOM.
sources.applicability: Web accessibility authoring guidance; useful interaction model for a desktop grid, but a native app must map equivalent semantics through its platform accessibility API.

critic_verification.review_note: Confirmed APG composite focus model, navigation/edit key split, and warning that an end command can stop at the last loaded DOM row.

reviser_review.review_note: Directly reopened. Confirmed composite grid focus, keyboard navigation/edit-mode handoff, and the warning that an end command can stop at the last loaded DOM row.

sources.title: Accessible Rich Internet Applications (WAI-ARIA) 1.2
sources.version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation, 2023-06-06 (version-pinned URL).
sources.locator: Roles grid and table; aria-rowcount / aria-rowindex / aria-colcount / aria-colindex; aria-selected; aria-sort; aria-readonly.
sources.observed_operation: Normative web accessibility semantics distinguish interactive grid from noninteractive table; partial DOM rows/columns can expose full counts and logical indexes. aria-selected indicates selection; aria-sort indicates sort order on a table/grid header; aria-readonly indicates editability, not navigability.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: For partial DOM, aria-rowcount/colcount represent full available totals (use -1 when unknown), with 1-based indexes for present rows/cells. aria-sort belongs on headers and should be on at most one header per grid. Apply only semantic states matching actual behavior.
sources.applicability: Normative WAI-ARIA requirements for web content/host languages; not a direct native desktop API contract.

critic_verification.review_note: Confirmed W3C Recommendation date and partial-DOM row count/index requirements; web semantics do not prescribe native APIs.

reviser_review.review_note: Directly reopened. Confirmed WAI-ARIA 1.2 is a 2023-06-06 Recommendation and partial-DOM counts/positions are specified for web content.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation, 2024-12-12 (version-pinned URL).
sources.locator: Success Criteria 2.1.1 Keyboard (A), 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA), 3.3.1 Error Identification (A), and 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA).
sources.observed_operation: Normative criteria require keyboard operation for all functionality, a visible focus indicator, text identification of input errors, and programmatically determinable status messages when markup-based status updates do not receive focus.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WCAG is scoped to web content; the exact criteria are not asserted as the governing legal standard for this unspecified desktop app. Their user outcomes remain design checks; native API equivalents and applicable obligations need an owner/platform decision.
sources.applicability: Use as a web-content target if that is the chosen delivery surface; otherwise treat as a useful baseline and verify OS accessibility contracts.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 3.3.1: Error Identification
sources.version_or_commit: Living WAI Understanding document; no pinned edition shown; consulted 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Intent and error identification examples, especially lines/sections requiring the identity of the item in error and describing errors in text.
sources.observed_operation: WAI explanatory guidance says an error description should provide its nature and identity of the item in error; text can be supplemented by color or an icon. An error list, inline message, alert, or dialog can be suitable depending on the situation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Informative explanation, not the normative WCAG text. HTML native validation may return focus to first invalid field but can show generic/nonpermanent messages and expose only the first error at a time.
sources.applicability: Supports a record-and-field-addressable error summary plus inline field explanation; native desktop implementation should expose equivalent text and focus behavior.

critic_verification.review_note: Confirmed WAI explanation requires nature and identity of the item in error; correction suggestions are a separate criterion.

reviser_review.review_note: Not directly reopened in this revision; critic independently reopened and confirmed the informative explanation of error identity and text.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 4.1.3: Status Messages
sources.version_or_commit: Living WAI Understanding document; no pinned edition shown; consulted 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Intent and definition of status messages; distinctions between result-set content and brief search completion/status text.
sources.observed_operation: Status updates that do not take focus may be exposed to assistive technology without moving focus. WAI distinguishes the actual result list from a brief message such as result count or search completion.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Applies to markup-language content. Do not treat every background record change as a status message; expose meaningful operation state/errors without flooding or interrupting the user.
sources.applicability: Guides aggregate announcements for filter/save/error status; platform-native notification/event mechanism must be tested if this is a native desktop application.

critic_verification.review_note: Confirmed markup status messages can be announced without focus; no basis to map this directly to unspecified native APIs.

sources.title: JavaScript Grid: Accessibility - AG Grid
sources.version_or_commit: AG Grid 36.2.0, explicitly shown on page.
sources.locator: ARIA Attributes; Ensure DOM Element order; Disable Group Sticky Rows; Ensure all grid elements are always rendered; Known Limitations.
sources.observed_operation: AG Grid uses row/column virtualization for performance. Its guidance recommends DOM order, avoiding sticky group rows for consistent indices, and disabling row/column virtualization or using pagination to ensure screen readers can inspect all rendered grid elements; disabling virtualization can grow DOM and slow rendering. It reports differences between screen-reader interpretation and recommends testing combinations.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: These are AG Grid vendor recommendations, not a universal ARIA rule. The 'disable virtualization' advice is explicitly balanced against performance and suggests pagination when needed.
sources.applicability: Useful implementation evidence and a warning about AT behavior; not a direct dependency recommendation for a native desktop console.

critic_verification.review_note: Confirmed AG Grid 36.2.0 guidance on pagination or disabled virtualization for full DOM availability and the rendering cost.

reviser_review.review_note: Directly reopened. AG Grid 36.2.0 recommends pagination for all elements in the current rendered rows to be available to screen readers; disabling virtualization for scrolling raises memory cost.

sources.title: Data Grid - Row definition - MUI X
sources.version_or_commit: Current MUI X documentation; page has no explicit release label in the retrieved text.

sources.title: Data Grid - Virtualization - MUI X v8
sources.version_or_commit: MUI X v8 documentation (versioned host path).

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Specific to MUI X v8 component limits and implementation; different products and versions may differ.
sources.applicability: Concrete perf/accessibility tradeoffs for virtualized renderer design, not a universal limit or recommendation.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Grid Pattern
sources.released_version_or_commit: Living APG guidance; no numbered release on page
sources.locator: About and data-grid pattern; keyboard interaction; setting focus inside cells; editing and navigating inside a cell; grid and table properties practice; lines 24-152
sources.observed_operation: Opened the pattern and used find/open around editing, selection, aria-selected, and keyboard boundary behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A grid is a composite only when its custom keyboard behavior is implemented. Arrow/Home/End and optional paging/navigation keys are defined; Enter/F2 can enter edit/widget mode, Escape can restore grid mode, and cell editors need their arrow-key behavior. Nonfunctional header cells need not be focusable. Selection uses aria-selected. Dynamically loaded rows can make Ctrl+End stop at the last DOM row rather than the last backend row.

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Focus is one moving point; selection can persist separately and may be multiple. APG says the selected state should be visually distinct from focus. sources.title: SQLite Transaction
sources.version_or_commit: SQLite official language documentation; rolling page, no version-specific snapshot shown.
sources.locator: Read transactions versus write transactions; DEFERRED/IMMEDIATE; Implicit versus explicit transactions, COMMIT behavior.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official SQLite documentation; inspected writer concurrency, transaction upgrade behavior, and SQLITE_BUSY at COMMIT.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Only one simultaneous write transaction is supported. A DEFERRED read transaction may fail to upgrade to a writer with SQLITE_BUSY; COMMIT may return SQLITE_BUSY and leave the transaction active.
sources.applicability: The import must define a bounded busy/retry or explicit rollback path and confirm commit/rollback state; concurrent changes require recomputing preview decisions.

sources.title: SQLite ON CONFLICT Clause
sources.version_or_commit: SQLite official language documentation; page states last updated 2025-11-22; no engine build is specified.
sources.locator: ABORT, FAIL, IGNORE, and REPLACE conflict-resolution algorithms.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official SQLite documentation; compared statement-level effects of each conflict algorithm.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: ABORT is default and backs out only the current statement while preserving prior transaction statements; FAIL can preserve earlier row changes in the failing statement; IGNORE skips affected rows; REPLACE deletes conflicting rows before insert.
sources.applicability: All-or-nothing import requires the application to explicitly roll back the outer transaction after an apply failure; the default statement conflict behavior alone is insufficient.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging and WAL-reset bug history

sources.locator: Overview, transaction atomicity across ATTACHed databases; Section 11, WAL-Reset Bug and its conditions/fixed versions.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official SQLite WAL page; inspected journal-mode scope, multi-database atomicity exception, affected versions, fixed releases, and required concurrency conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL-reset defect affects WAL databases through 3.51.2 and requires at least two connections to the same database plus coincident write/checkpoint activity. WAL transactions across multiple ATTACHed databases are not atomic as a set. Rollback-journal mode is SQLite default.
sources.applicability: Keep the release floor conditional on WAL and the supported connection pattern; if WAL is selected, pin a fixed version/backport and test. Keep all accepted rows and provenance in one database file if the design promises atomicity.

sources.title: Linux kernel Control Group v2 documentation
sources.version_or_commit: latest documentation alias; exact kernel documentation revision was not surfaced. Accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Basic Operations/Availability and Enabling (lines 145-173); Resource Distribution Models (210-242); cpu.weight/cpu.max (568-601); memory.max (711-722); io.max (1388-1416); pids.max (1560-1595). Core Interface Files cgroup.kill (lines 480-489).
sources.observed_behavior: Controllers are not enabled by default; availability is conditional on kernel support and no v1 binding. Controllers are enabled top-down. CPU weights distribute to active eligible work; cpu.weight defaults to 100. cpu.max defaults to unlimited. memory.max defaults to max and can invoke the OOM killer; usage may temporarily exceed it. io.max is per device; pids.max is a process count hard limit. cgroup.kill kills the cgroup and descendants via SIGKILL and handles concurrent forks; it exists on non-root cgroups and fails for threaded cgroups.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Host must expose cgroup v2 controllers, enable them in the hierarchy, and delegate configuration rights; weights are not a queue-aging guarantee. Resource controls are hierarchical.
sources.applicability: Linux process-tree resource controls where the editor/service has the required delegation. Not a cross-platform sandbox or an unconditional guarantee.

sources.title: Wasmtime Config fuel and epoch interruption

sources.title: Linux kernel Landlock: unprivileged access control
sources.version_or_commit: latest kernel documentation alias; exact kernel documentation revision not surfaced. Landlock first introduced in Linux 5.13.
sources.locator: Ruleset enforcement and no_new_privs (lines 205-228); file-descriptor rights (279-282); compatibility/ABI check (283-307); build/boot support (877-883); network access-right ABI introductions (438-468, 843-870).
sources.observed_behavior: Landlock lets a process add an irreversible, additive access policy for itself and subsequent children; per-directory filesystem rules and network rights are explicit. The current thread and inherited file descriptors have conditions that affect coverage.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Linux 5.13+ with CONFIG_SECURITY_LANDLOCK built and LSM enabled at boot. Check ABI at runtime; unprivileged enforcement requires no_new_privs. Some rights, network controls and thread synchronization appeared only in later ABIs. Existing file descriptors can retain access granted before enforcement; start in a fresh single-thread worker and close unneeded inherited handles.
sources.applicability: Linux filesystem/network confinement option to pair with cgroup resources; cannot be promised on every kernel/boot configuration.

sources.title: Linux setsid(2) manual page
sources.version_or_commit: Linux man-pages page; exact page release could not be confirmed because the direct open timed out. The retrieved page states POSIX.1-2024 conformance; no commit SHA was observed.
sources.locator: DESCRIPTION: a caller that is not a process-group leader can create a new session and process group and becomes their sole initial member. NOTES: forked children inherit the session ID. Direct open was attempted but timed out; the search result exposed these sections.
observed_operation: web.open (timed out; no page body returned)
sources.observed_behavior: setsid() succeeds for a caller that is not already a process-group leader, creating a new session and process group; the caller is initially the only member. A child normally inherits its parent's session ID, but a non-group-leader child can create a separate session/group. Thus signalling only the worker's original process group does not prove all descendants were terminated.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: setsid() fails when the caller is already a process-group leader. A forked child whose PID differs from the inherited process-group ID can meet the non-leader condition. This describes Linux/POSIX process/session semantics; cgroup membership and Windows Job Object behavior are separate mechanisms.
sources.applicability: Directly qualifies the proposal to treat process-group termination as sufficient teardown for an untrusted converter. Use cgroup/job membership or another verified per-platform mechanism for a whole-job guarantee; do not generalize this Linux finding to other platforms.

sources.title: Linux kernel Control Group v2 documentation
sources.version_or_commit: latest documentation alias; exact kernel documentation revision was not surfaced. Accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Basic Operations/Availability and Enabling (lines 145-173); Resource Distribution Models (210-242); cpu.weight/cpu.max (568-601); memory.max (711-722); io.max (1388-1416); pids.max (1560-1595). Core Interface Files cgroup.kill (lines 480-489).
sources.observed_behavior: Controllers are not enabled by default; availability is conditional on kernel support and no v1 binding. Controllers are enabled top-down. CPU weights distribute to active eligible work; cpu.weight defaults to 100. cpu.max defaults to unlimited. memory.max defaults to max and can invoke the OOM killer; usage may temporarily exceed it. io.max is per device; pids.max is a process count hard limit. cgroup.kill kills the cgroup and descendants via SIGKILL and handles concurrent forks; it exists on non-root cgroups and fails for threaded cgroups.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Host must expose cgroup v2 controllers, enable them in the hierarchy, and delegate configuration rights; weights are not a queue-aging guarantee. Resource controls are hierarchical.
sources.applicability: Linux process-tree resource controls where the editor/service has the required delegation. Not a cross-platform sandbox or an unconditional guarantee.

reviser_independent_check.observed_behavior: Reopened the official current kernel cgroup v2 documentation. It says every process belongs to one cgroup, children are born into their parent cgroup, controllers are conditional on support and top-down enablement, limits may be overcommitted, cpu.weight distributes among active children, and io.max is a device throughput limit.
reviser_independent_check.governing_condition_default_exception: The check confirms the original applicability conditions: host support, hierarchy, delegation, and process membership still matter. No target host was inspected.
reviser_independent_check.applicability: Independent source recheck only; no runtime or host enforcement test.

sources.title: Linux rename(2) manual page
sources.version_or_commit: Linux man-pages 6.19, dated 2026-02-08; rename is also specified by POSIX.1-2024.
sources.locator: DESCRIPTION (atomic replacement); ERRORS (EXDEV); BUGS (NFS failure/retry ambiguity).
sources.observed_behavior: Replacing an existing target is atomic for pathname visibility; cross-mounted-filesystem rename fails with EXDEV. NFS may report failure after the server performed the rename.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Linux/POSIX pathname semantics and underlying filesystem; atomic visibility is not the same as crash durability or a transaction over a multi-file bundle.
sources.applicability: Linux same-filesystem local publish primitive; destination adapters must account for cross-volume and network semantics.

sources.title: Windows ReplaceFileW
sources.version_or_commit: Microsoft Learn Win32 API page; path rules include Windows 10 version 1607 behavior.
sources.locator: Remarks lines 120-143; error codes for partial replacement; REPLACEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH unsupported; same-volume requirement.
sources.observed_behavior: The function combines replacement steps, preserves attributes/ACLs in supported conditions, and may have partial-failure states; all relevant files must be on the same volume.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Path length behavior depends on Windows version/opt-in. Write-through is unsupported; check return code and GetLastError and do not assume failure means no rename occurred.
sources.applicability: Windows same-volume replacement primitive; destination commit and error recovery still belong to the coordinator.

sources.title: Linux fsync(2) manual page
sources.version_or_commit: Linux man-pages 6.19, dated 2026-02-08; POSIX.1-2024.
sources.locator: DESCRIPTION and ERRORS (file data/metadata flush, directory entry caveat, late NFS/ENOSPC/EDQUOT).
sources.observed_behavior: fsync on a file does not necessarily persist the containing directory entry; a separate directory fsync may be required. Some network filesystems may report storage quota/space failures after a write.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Filesystem and device implement durability semantics; sync success is not a universal guarantee across network/object-storage destinations.
sources.applicability: Linux crash-durability guidance for local file commit; do not confuse durability with successful transfer or artifact verification.

sources.title: Windows AppContainer isolation
sources.version_or_commit: Microsoft Learn Win32 documentation, last updated 2025-07-08.
sources.locator: File isolation, network isolation and process isolation, lines 31-47.
sources.observed_behavior: AppContainer isolation is based on least privilege; access to files/registry can be granted narrowly, network access is granular, and process-object isolation limits cross-process influence.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Access is only to granted resources; exact compatibility depends on app type and supported Windows versions. It is an access-control sandbox, not the Job Object resource budget.
sources.applicability: Windows sandbox access-control layer to pair with per-job Job Objects.

sources.title: Linux kernel Landlock: unprivileged access control
sources.version_or_commit: latest kernel documentation alias; exact kernel documentation revision not surfaced. Landlock first introduced in Linux 5.13.
sources.locator: Ruleset enforcement and no_new_privs (lines 205-228); file-descriptor rights (279-282); compatibility/ABI check (283-307); build/boot support (877-883); network access-right ABI introductions (438-468, 843-870).
sources.observed_behavior: Landlock lets a process add an irreversible, additive access policy for itself and subsequent children; per-directory filesystem rules and network rights are explicit. The current thread and inherited file descriptors have conditions that affect coverage.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Linux 5.13+ with CONFIG_SECURITY_LANDLOCK built and LSM enabled at boot. Check ABI at runtime; unprivileged enforcement requires no_new_privs. Some rights, network controls and thread synchronization appeared only in later ABIs. Existing file descriptors can retain access granted before enforcement; start in a fresh single-thread worker and close unneeded inherited handles.
sources.applicability: Linux filesystem/network confinement option to pair with cgroup resources; cannot be promised on every kernel/boot configuration.

sources.title: Pandoc User Guide security note
sources.version_or_commit: Current Pandoc User Guide alias; exact release/commit not fixed on the page.
sources.locator: A note on security, lines 4867-4883; filter/custom-writer filesystem capability and --sandbox scope.
sources.observed_behavior: The manual warns filters/custom writers can perform arbitrary filesystem operations; --sandbox affects readers/writers only, and combining it with filters or PDF engines leaves security risks.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Claim is specific to Pandoc sandbox behavior and cited filter/custom-writer extension points; it is not a general sandbox API guarantee.
sources.applicability: Evidence for why an external converter/filter must be treated as executable code and separately contained.

sources.title: Linux setsid(2) manual page
sources.version_or_commit: Linux man-pages page; exact page release could not be confirmed because the direct open timed out. The retrieved page states POSIX.1-2024 conformance; no commit SHA was observed.
sources.locator: DESCRIPTION: a caller that is not a process-group leader can create a new session and process group and becomes their sole initial member. NOTES: forked children inherit the session ID. Direct open was attempted but timed out; the search result exposed these sections.
observed_operation: web.open (timed out; no page body returned)
sources.observed_behavior: setsid() succeeds for a caller that is not already a process-group leader, creating a new session and process group; the caller is initially the only member. A child normally inherits its parent's session ID, but a non-group-leader child can create a separate session/group. Thus signalling only the worker's original process group does not prove all descendants were terminated.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: setsid() fails when the caller is already a process-group leader. A forked child whose PID differs from the inherited process-group ID can meet the non-leader condition. This describes Linux/POSIX process/session semantics; cgroup membership and Windows Job Object behavior are separate mechanisms.
sources.applicability: Directly qualifies the proposal to treat process-group termination as sufficient teardown for an untrusted converter. Use cgroup/job membership or another verified per-platform mechanism for a whole-job guarantee; do not generalize this Linux finding to other platforms.

reviser_independent_check.observed_behavior: The search result returned the manual text: setsid() creates a session/process group only for a caller that is not already a process-group leader; a forked child inherits the session ID. A non-group-leader child can call setsid and leave the original process group.
reviser_independent_check.governing_condition_default_exception: Direct open of the original S22 URL timed out. The search result was the same Linux manual page on the www.man7.org host alias; the original S22 URL and source identity are preserved.
reviser_independent_check.applicability: Confirms that signaling the worker original process group alone does not prove Linux descendant teardown; it does not establish cgroup, Windows, or macOS behavior.

sources.title: The SGI XFS Filesystem — Linux Kernel documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Current kernel documentation alias; exact kernel documentation revision not surfaced.
sources.locator: Mount options `uquota`/`usrquota` lines 109-112 and `pquota`/`prjquota` lines 119-122.
sources.observed_behavior: The documentation says user and project disk-quota accounting may be enabled, and limits may be enforced; project quota uses the pquota/prjquota mount option.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Quota accounting/enforcement is filesystem- and mount-configuration-dependent; the documentation explicitly describes enforcement as optional. This is an example mechanism, not a portable default.
sources.applicability: Illustrates a Linux scratch-capacity option that could back a per-job scratch area, while reinforcing the need for host-specific support and configuration.

reviser_independent_check.observed_behavior: The official kernel documentation search result identifies uquota/usrquota and pquota/prjquota as enabling quota accounting with limits optionally enforced; no portable default is implied.
reviser_independent_check.applicability: Supports XFS as a conditional example only; no filesystem quota was configured or tested.

sources.title: XPC — Apple Developer Documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Current Apple Developer documentation; no semantic version or commit shown.
sources.locator: Overview and service-type table in the indexed page result: launchd-managed helper services, privilege isolation, and XPC Service process-per-client/lifetime description.
sources.observed_behavior: The indexed official page summary describes XPC as lightweight IPC for helper tools and privilege isolation, with an XPC Service process per client tied to the client lifetime. Opening the page rendered a JavaScript-only shell; following its Markdown link failed with an unsupported-content-type error, so the indexed summary was the readable evidence.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Service lifecycle and isolation depend on the selected XPC service type and configuration. The documentation does not establish per-converter resource quotas or show that arbitrary separately installed converters can be bundled as XPC services.
sources.applicability: A macOS privilege-separation alternative to assess as a host-owned broker; it is not itself evidence of hard CPU, memory or disk limits.

reviser_independent_check.observed_behavior: The current official Apple result describes XPC helper IPC, privilege isolation, launchd management, and an XPC Service process per client tied to client lifetime; it says this service type is bundled in an app/framework.
reviser_independent_check.applicability: Supports a macOS helper/broker alternative, not arbitrary dynamic converter entitlements, per-export teardown, or hard resource quotas.

sources.title: Process — Apple Developer Documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Current Apple Developer documentation; no semantic version or commit shown.
sources.locator: Creating and initializing a process; sandboxed-app helper behavior, as exposed in the indexed result.
sources.observed_behavior: The indexed official page summary states that a child process launched from a sandboxed app inherits the parent app sandbox and points to XPC services for helpers that need different sandbox entitlements. Opening the page rendered a JavaScript-only shell; following its Markdown link failed with an unsupported-content-type error, so the indexed summary was the readable evidence.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Applies to Process-launched children from a sandboxed macOS app as described by Apple. It does not imply that all macOS subprocesses share an identical configuration or that XPC provides resource quotas.
sources.applicability: Supports evaluating the actual per-export helper entitlement boundary and avoids assuming process separation alone yields a narrower macOS sandbox.

reviser_independent_check.observed_behavior: The current official Apple result says a Process-launched child of a sandboxed app inherits its sandbox and points to XPC services when a helper needs different entitlements.
reviser_independent_check.applicability: Supports comparing helper entitlement boundaries; it does not establish a process-tree termination or resource-quota guarantee.
